subject: Unexpected error for obsCov in UnmarkedFramePcount

messages.author: 7a9514c5573993b1
messages.subject: Unexpected error for obsCov in UnmarkedFramePcount
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to format my data for a survey about Ortalis vetula in Guatemala. At the simple stage of unmarkedFramePcount, I am getting an error and I cannot figure out why!

This is the code an error:

> umf.datos4 <- unmarkedFramePCount(
+     y = datos4[,1:3],
+     siteCovs = datos4[,4:9],
+     obsCovs = list(date = datos4[,10:12],time = datos4[,13:15])
+ )
Error in unmarkedFrame(y, siteCovs, obsCovs, obsToY = diag(J), mapInfo = mapInfo) : 
  At least one element of obsCovs is not a matrix or data frame.
In addition: Warning message:
In if (!(class(obsCovs[[i]]) %in% c("matrix", "data.frame"))) stop("At least one element of obsCovs is not a matrix or data frame.") :
  the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used

The data I am using is linked to this post. What am I doing wrong when formatting the data for obsCov?

Thanks

Gabrielle

messages.author: d7383a0b1c5b64d0
messages.subject: Re: Unexpected error for obsCov in UnmarkedFramePcount
parts:
Hi Gabrielle,

Glad you got it working.  I don't know why it would work in R when not running through RStudio, but not in RStudio.  However, I am able to reproduce your error in RStudio by giving the datos4 dataframe the additional classes of 'tbl' and 'tbl_df' (which it seems your datos4 object had, based on the output you posted).  Things in tibble format sometimes behave a little differently from things that are just plain 'data.frames' (even though tibbles are also 'data.frames').  So, to get rid of the 'tbl' and 'tbl_df' classes, I ran as.data.frame().

datos4 <- as.data.frame(datos4)
str(datos4)
umf.datos4 <- unmarkedFramePCount(y = datos4[,1:3],
                                  siteCovs = datos4[,4:9],
                                  obsCovs = list(date = datos4[,10:12],
                                                 time = datos4[,13:15]))


After running as.data.frame(), the output of those str() command shows that the only class is 'data.frame', and the call to unmarkedFramePcount() no longer produces an error (at least for me). 

Cheers,
Willson
